question: According to the classification of modern Indian languages, which linguistic family accounts for the largest share of the Indian population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-European (Aryan)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indo-European (Aryan) linguistic family accounts for the largest share of the Indian population, encompassing major languages like Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, and Urdu.
 
• Approximately 70% of India's population speaks languages belonging to the Indo-European family.
 
• The Indo-European family of languages originated from a common ancestral language known as Proto-Indo-European, which spread across Europe and South Asia.
 
• Hindi, a major Indo-European language, is the most widely spoken language in India and serves as one of the official languages of the Indian government.
 
• The Indo-European linguistic family in India is primarily concentrated in the northern, central, and western regions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sino-Tibetan (Kirata):** Languages in this family include Manipuri, Bodo, and other tribal languages in northeastern India. It accounts for a smaller share of the population compared to Indo-European and Dravidian families.
 
• **Dravidian:** This linguistic family is prominent in southern India, including languages like Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam. It is the second-largest linguistic family in India.
 
• **Austric (Nishada):** Includes languages like Santali and Mundari, primarily spoken by tribal communities in eastern and central India.
 
• **Indo-European Spread:** The Indo-European languages spread to India during ancient migrations and later evolved into many distinct languages, forming the largest linguistic group in the country.
 
• **Language Demographics:** Census data and linguistic studies consistently show the dominance of Indo-European languages in India's population distribution.
